newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sorghum could feel pressure - GRAINCO.
newsitem.headline: Australia sorghum could feel pressure - GRAINCO.

text.p: Domestic Australian sorghum values could come under pressure if a large winter planting takes place, particularly in southern Queensland, Queensland grain co-operative Grainco Ltd said in its weekly market report.
Pressure would be increased if the planting was early, based on rain received in many parts of the region, it said.
The domestic sorghum market finished last week at about A$138.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane, reflecting values of about A$120.00 a tonne on farm.
Rain during the week supported the market as lack of grower selling meant some late February positions were a little difficult to cover, trading manager Rob Brealey said..
"Fine weather and good harvest conditions over the coming weeks could see values remain stable, although the market will be closely monitoring the level of grower selling," he said.
After a week of firming values, the market continued to wait for harvest to get into full swing before making further assumptions about grower selling, he said.
The longer-term international outlook remained bearish with reports of increased U.S. corn planting intentions, he said.
Pressure on international values would occur particularly if the U.S. corn crop was planted without major problems, he said.
Recent rain had taken a toll on likely Australian cottonseed production, which would be tight again this year, he said.
The prospect of a record Australian cotton crop may pressure prices and storage, he said.
The price outlook for the longer term appeared reasonably stable. If the Australian dollar does not rise further domestic prices should remain at current levels, he said.
"The next hurdle to confront prices will be that of ginning pressure," he said.
Barley markets remained quiet, although export values would depend on crop prospects in the northern hemisphere and southern Australia, he said.
The possibility of a sizeable barley planting in southern Queensland this year could cause domestic prices to be steady to slightly lower over coming months, he said.
The malting barley market was looking for price support on import demand from China in April/May, he said.
New crop price indications were about A$170.00 a tonne Brisbane, he said.
